2027-01-02.title: Saturday after New Year · Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios
readings: The Lord's servant must be kindly to everyone
You must be born from above
2027-01-02.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. Name day of Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis Catholicos. Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of Mavelikara (2007). Mar Macarios the Solitary (Ihidoyo).
2027-01-02.verse: Jesus answered, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
theo: Today the Church remembers Mar Baselios (St Basil the Great) and Mar Gregorios (St Gregory Nazianzen), friends and bishops of Cappadocia who defended faith in the Holy Trinity, and whose names are borne by our Catholicos and many of our bishops. It is the name day of Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis Catholicos; we pray for him and for the Eparchy of Mavelikara, erected on this day in 2007.

In the Gospel Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him: “no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.” A few days before Denho, the feast of Jesus' baptism, we are reminded of our own: a new birth from above. Jesus also says that the Son of Man must be lifted up, as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness. Paul tells Timothy that the Lord's servant “must not be quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient.” Basil and Gregory were exactly this: firm in the truth, gentle with people.
outline: Ask: what does it mean to be born again?
Basil, Gregory and every servant of the Lord.
live: Pray today for our Catholicos and the bishops of our Church.
If you must correct someone today, do it with gentleness.
2027-01-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you call us to be born from above of water and the Spirit. Through the prayers of Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios, keep our Catholicos and bishops faithful and gentle shepherds, and renew in us the grace of our Baptism. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is offered for the Catholicos and the bishops by name. Today we pray especially for Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis on his name day.

quick: Basil and Gregory defended the Trinity and were gentle shepherds.
We must be born of water and Spirit.
The Son of Man is lifted up to give eternal life.
2027-01-02.action: Pray today for our Catholicos and bishops.
2027-01-02.question: Do I live as one born from above?

family.explain: A teacher named Nicodemus came to Jesus at night. Jesus told him: you must be born again, from water and the Holy Spirit. That happens in Baptism!
family.intention: We pray for our Catholicos and bishops.
family.ask: Ask: “Where were you baptised? Who are your godparents?”

illus: A retired headmaster in Mavelikara was known for one habit: he never corrected a student in front of others. He would call the boy aside, speak quietly, and end with a blessing. Decades later his old students said they remembered his gentleness more than his lessons.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you told Nicodemus that we must be born from above. Renew in us the grace of our Baptism as we gather. Amen.
share: No one can enter the kingdom without being born of water and Spirit (John 3:5). How do I live my Baptism?
The Son of Man must be lifted up (John 3:14). What does the Cross mean to me?
The Lord's servant must be kindly to everyone (2 Timothy 2:24). How can I correct others with gentleness?
pm.resp: Lord, renew us by your Spirit.
interc: For our Catholicos, Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, on his name day.
For the Eparchy of Mavelikara and all our eparchies.
For teachers and catechists, that they may be gentle and patient.
For those seeking God by night, like Nicodemus.
For our group, that we may live as people born from above.
pm.close: Father, through water and the Spirit you gave us new birth. Through the prayers of Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios, keep us faithful to the faith of the Church and gentle with all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we honour Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios, two great bishops of Cappadocia in the fourth century. They were close friends who defended faith in the Holy Trinity. Our Catholicos bears the name Baselios, and today is his name day. We pray for him and for the Eparchy of Mavelikara.

In the Gospel Nicodemus, a respected teacher, comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him: no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit (John 3:5). Nicodemus is puzzled. How can an old man be born again? Jesus speaks of a birth from above, a gift of God.
In a few days we celebrate Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Jesus' baptism opens the way for ours. In Baptism we were born of water and Spirit and became children of God.
Jesus also says: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). The new life flows from the Cross.

Paul gives Timothy a portrait of a good shepherd: not quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient, correcting opponents with gentleness (2 Timothy 2:24–25). That was Basil and Gregory. May it be our Catholicos, our bishops, our priests, and every parent and teacher. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said we must be born again from water and the Holy Spirit. That happened when you were baptised! Today let us pray for our Catholicos, Baselios Bava.

intro: Theme: “No one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.”
New birth from above, the lifted-up Son, and gentle shepherds.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
Jesus answered, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises before Denho.

q: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.”
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
points.apply: Spend a few minutes looking at the Cross in silence today.

sub: Firm in truth, kind to all.
q: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
And the Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient, correcting opponents with gentleness.
points.apply: Pray for our Catholicos and correct others gently.

concl: Born of water and Spirit, we look to the Cross.
Like Basil and Gregory, let us be firm in faith and gentle in love.
2027-01-02.resolve: Pray each day this week for our Catholicos and bishops.
